facts.text: On this date in 1991, hardliners staged a coup against Gorbachev. It collapsed in 60 hours — but the USSR itself followed within four months.
On August 19, 1960, a Soviet court sentenced U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers to 10 years. He was exchanged for a KGB spy just 21 months later.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires than any country on Earth — roughly one in three residents qualifies — yet it maintains its own sovereign military.
The Philippines is the only country in Asia where divorce remains fully illegal, a legacy of Spanish colonial law that 400 years of independence has not overturned.
Istanbul sits in two continents simultaneously. More people live on its European side, but the Asian side is larger in area — and growing faster.
On this date in 1999, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt — not foreign — triggering a ruble collapse that wiped out a generation of middle-class savings in weeks.
On August 19, 1982, the Dow closed below 777. Within two years it had doubled. The greatest bull market in American history began on a day most investors were too scared to notice.
The S&P 500 has returned roughly 10% annually for a century — but the average investor has earned closer to 4%, entirely due to buying high and selling low.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion valuation in 2019. That single company was worth more than the entire stock markets of Germany and France combined.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792. The original 24 brokers agreed to charge each other fixed commissions — essentially forming a cartel on day one.
On this date in 1960, Sputnik 5 returned Belka and Strelka to Earth — the first living creatures to orbit and come back alive, paving the way for Gagarin nine months later.
Your bones are constantly dissolving and rebuilding themselves. Every decade, you have an almost entirely new skeleton.
On August 19, 1839, Daguerre's photographic process was released to the world for free. The French government bought the patent and gave it, in their words, as a gift to all humanity.
A teaspoon of neutron star material weighs roughly a billion tons. Its gravity is so intense that the star's surface features are never taller than five centimeters.
The mantis shrimp sees with 16 types of color receptors — four times more than humans — yet processes color worse. It identifies hues by timing nerve pulses, not mixing signals.
On this day in 1839, France gave photography to the world — Louis Daguerre's process was released publicly, free for all. The Eiffel Tower didn't exist yet, but now Paris could be captured forever.
On this day in 1934, Germans voted to merge the offices of Chancellor and President, handing Hitler total power. The referendum passed with 89.9% approval.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed. You could transmit a document across a wire before you could reliably cross the continent by train.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was born roughly 2,500 years after Khufu's tomb was sealed.
The University of Oxford began teaching around 1096 — making it older than the Aztec Empire, which wasn't founded until 1428. Oxford was already ancient history when Tenochtitlan was built.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast linguists now treat it as a legitimate neologism.
Hiraeth (n.): Welsh for a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or never had. Untranslatable, it folds grief, longing, and belonging into a single syllable cluster.

On this day in 1839, the daguerreotype process was released to the public in Paris. The French word 'photographie' entered English within weeks, fusing Greek roots for light (phōs) and writing (graphē).

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the wordless look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Guinness once listed it as the most concise word on Earth.

On August 19, 1960, the USSR sentenced U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers — and the incident cemented 'espionage' in Cold War vocabulary, a word borrowed from French espionnage, itself from Old Italian spia, meaning spy.
On August 19, 2020, Uniswap v2 had been live for 3 months and was processing more daily volume than Coinbase Pro — a DEX had quietly outtraded a major centralized exchange for the first time.
On August 19, 2018, ETH bottomed near $185 after falling 93% from its January peak — the same asset that would settle over $11 trillion in on-chain volume during 2021.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat disabled in the codebase for three years before being activated in BIP 65 in 2015 — Satoshi had written it in but never switched it on.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but embedded directly in the coinbase transaction's scriptSig field, making it immutable chain history.

Ethereum validators earn MEV-boost rewards that routinely exceed base block rewards; on high-traffic days, a single block proposer can collect more from MEV than the protocol itself pays out in issuance.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet — its 15.3% error rate was so far below second place (26.2%) that the computer vision community initially suspected a bug.
On this date in 2019, OpenAI released a staged rollout of GPT-2 citing misuse concerns — a decision widely mocked at the time, then quietly vindicated by every subsequent model release cycle.
The original transformer paper, 'Attention Is All You Need,' lists eight authors. Google filed no patent on it, a decision that may represent the most expensive IP omission in software history.

Chinchilla scaling laws (2022) showed that most large language models of their era were undertrained relative to their parameter count — meaning labs had been spending compute budgets in roughly the wrong ratio for years.
RLHF, the technique that made ChatGPT usable, was first described in a 2017 OpenAI paper about training agents to play Atari games. The word 'language' does not appear in it.
